rationale: The two are nearly identical: the same name-to-grade dict, sorting with a (grade, name) key and an added history list. A has two small advantages. Its added() returns a copy of the internal list, so callers cannot mutate the object's state, whereas B exposes the private list directly. Its add_student computes the outcome once and has a single append/return path instead of duplicating the append-and-return logic in two branches. B's inline comment documenting the dict's shape is helpful, and its one-liners are compact. On balance A is a bit more robust and less repetitive.
